overview: Capricorn Metals is a Western Australian gold producer operating the Karlawinda Gold Project (KGP) in the Pilbara, which poured first gold in June 2021 and produced a record 123,589oz in FY2026 at an AISC of $1,629/oz. The company is now transitioning from a single-mine producer to a multi-mine gold developer, expanding KGP via the Karlawinda Expansion Project (KEP, commissioning FY2027) and advancing the much larger Mt Gibson Gold Project (MGGP) in the Murchison region, targeting combined production of 400,000+ ounces per annum under its 'Range 500' aspiration (500,000oz/year within 5 years). Capricorn is debt-free, unhedged, and paid its maiden dividend in FY2026.

business_model.summary: Single-commodity gold producer generating revenue entirely from gold sales at spot/realised prices, with no hedge book. FY2026 revenue of $711.4m was driven by record production (123,589oz) and a record realised gold price of $6,241/oz, up from $2,471/oz in FY2022. Growth capital ($300.7m in FY2026, tripled year-on-year) is self-funded from KGP operating cash flow, avoiding equity dilution or debt for the KEP and early MGGP works. The company began returning capital via its first dividend (10cps fully franked, $45.7m) in FY2026 while simultaneously funding its largest-ever growth capex program.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - gold sold to bullion refiners/traders at prevailing market/spot prices; no offtake concentration risk typical of industrial commodities
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Western Australia (Pilbara - KGP; Murchison - MGGP and Golden Range/Warriedar tenements); revenue realised in AUD, gold priced in USD globally

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-tier ASX gold producer (~$5-6bn market cap) with a single low-cost, long-life operating mine (KGP, >10 year mine life) and a large-scale, high-grade development pipeline (MGGP, 19-year mine life at 260,000ozpa steady state) that would elevate it toward the scale of Evolution Mining or Regis Resources once in production.

moat_factors.description: AISC of $1,629/oz in FY2026 remains among the lowest in the Australian gold industry, preserving margin leverage to a high gold price; being unhedged means 100% upside participation, unlike peers still working through legacy hedge books
Debt-free with $504.8m net cash at FY2026 year-end, enabling KEP and MGGP to be funded entirely from internal cash flow without dilutive capital raises

Group Ore Reserves of 5.2Moz (KGP 1.57Moz + MGGP 3.67Moz including maiden underground reserve) and Mineral Resources of ~8.7Moz provide long-dated production visibility (KGP >10 years, MGGP ~19 years)
Deep operational knowledge of WA Pilbara/Murchison geology and permitting processes, reducing execution risk versus greenfield or offshore expansion

weaknesses: Single operating asset (KGP) until MGGP reaches production - concentrated operational and geological risk relative to diversified multi-mine peers
No hedging means full exposure to gold price downside as well as upside, unlike peers who have locked in some price protection
Smaller scale than Northern Star (~$31bn market cap) or Evolution Mining limits index weighting, trading liquidity and ability to absorb large-scale M&A
Execution risk on two concurrent, capital-intensive growth projects (KEP commissioning, MGGP construction) increases the chance of cost overruns or delays

growth_drivers: Karlawinda Expansion Project (KEP) - processing capacity increase from ~4Mtpa to 6.5Mtpa, lifting KGP average annual production to ~150,000oz; commissioning commenced Q1 FY2027

Mt Gibson Gold Project (MGGP) development - PFS confirms 260,000ozpa steady-state production (including underground mining for the first time) over a 19-year mine life at industry-leading low AISC; Commonwealth (EPBC Act) environmental approval received June 2026; targeting commencement of development activities in the December 2026 quarter, subject to remaining WA state approvals
'Range 500' aspiration - combined KGP + MGGP production target of 500,000oz per annum within five years, positioning Capricorn among the larger ASX-listed pure-gold producers

Warriedar Resources acquisition (completed November 2025) - added the Golden Range Project and Ricciardo gold-antimony deposit, expanding the WA resource base by ~25% and providing satellite ore sources near MGGP

Continued near-mine and regional exploration - record FY2026 drilling (378 holes/81,449m at KGP; 1,953 holes/235,311m at MGGP) converting Inferred to Indicated/Reserve categories and extending mine life via underground potential (Orion South underground MRE of 895koz)
Structural gold price tailwind - realised price rose from $2,471/oz (FY2022) to $6,241/oz (FY2026), materially expanding margins even as AISC has risen

business.description: Until MGGP reaches commercial production, essentially all cash flow depends on KGP; any operational disruption, pit slope failure, or grade/recovery shortfall at KGP has outsized earnings impact

AISC has climbed from ~$1,112/oz (FY2022) to $1,629/oz (FY2026) and FY2027 guidance is $1,900-2,100/oz, reflecting cost inflation, higher strip ratios and lower ore mined; if gold prices retreat, margin compression could be rapid
Simultaneously commissioning KEP and advancing MGGP construction/permitting increases risk of cost overruns, schedule slippage or capital misallocation

financial.description: FY2026 growth capex tripled to $300.7m and MGGP construction will require substantial further capital; while currently self-funded from cash flow, a sustained gold price pullback could pressure the fully-funded development thesis
No hedge book means 100% of revenue is exposed to spot gold price volatility in both directions - a benefit in a rising market but a risk if prices reverse

The maiden FY2026 dividend (10cps, $45.7m) competes with heavy growth capex requirements; balancing shareholder returns against MGGP funding needs could pressure the payout in future years if commodity prices soften

regulatory.description: Federal EPBC approval was received in June 2026, but final Western Australian state approvals (Part IV EP Act) remain outstanding, with the Environmental Review Document submitted July 2026; delays could push back the targeted December 2026 quarter development start

regulatory.risk: Native title, heritage and environmental compliance
regulatory.description: Both KGP and MGGP require ongoing management of Traditional Owner agreements, biodiversity approvals and tailings/water management; conditions attached to approvals could constrain mine planning

macro.description: Company's record profitability is heavily geared to the gold price rally (realised price +153% since FY2022); a sustained pullback in gold (e.g., from faster-than-expected Fed tightening, US dollar strength, or reduced central bank buying) would compress margins given rising AISC
WA mining sector labour, diesel, and contractor cost inflation continues to pressure AISC across the industry
Gold is priced in USD globally; AUD revenue benefits from a weaker Australian dollar, but a stronger AUD would be a modest headwind

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold price forecasts for 2026-2027 remain broadly bullish: J.P. Morgan projects gold approaching $6,000/oz by end-2026 (potentially $6,300/oz in 2027), while Goldman Sachs forecasts ~$4,900/oz by end-2026, both citing central bank accumulation, Fed rate cuts reducing the opportunity cost of holding gold, and structural de-dollarization. Central bank buying has moderated in early 2026 (net purchases of only ~16 tonnes in Q1 2026 versus a 2021-2025 average of ~225 tonnes/quarter) but UBS still expects 750-1,000 tonnes of annual buying and considers the structural bull market intact.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - gold mining earnings are highly levered to the gold price cycle; Capricorn's unhedged position amplifies both upside and downside relative to hedged peers
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High (indirect) - gold as a non-yielding asset benefits from falling real interest rates/Fed easing, which has been a primary driver of the current price rally
key_input_costs: Labour and contractor costs (WA mining sector wage inflation)
Steel/consumables for TSF and plant construction

recent_developments.event: Reported record FY2026 results: sales revenue $769.3m (gold sales), underlying EBITDA $483.6m (+63% YoY), underlying NPAT $327.2m (+59% YoY), net cash of $504.8m (+$149m), and declared maiden fully franked dividend of 10cps ($45.7m/$22.8m paid in year)
Group Ore Reserve updated to 5.2Moz (KGP 1.57Moz +32%, MGGP 3.67Moz including maiden 365koz underground reserve); Group Mineral Resource increased to ~8.7Moz

Released updated Mt Gibson Gold Project Pre-Feasibility Study confirming 260,000ozpa steady-state production over a 19-year mine life, incorporating underground mining for the first time, with a pre-tax NPV of ~A$6.1bn at A$5,500/oz gold

Received Commonwealth (EPBC Act) environmental approval for MGGP from the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water - a major permitting milestone; remaining WA state approvals (Part IV EP Act) still required, with the Environmental Review Document submitted July 2026

Completed acquisition of Warriedar Resources Limited, adding the Golden Range Project (including the Ricciardo gold-antimony deposit) approximately 90km north of MGGP, expanding the WA resource base by ~25%
Board approved the Karlawinda Expansion Project (KEP), increasing KGP processing capacity from ~4Mtpa to 6.5Mtpa; construction proceeded through FY2026 with commissioning commencing Q1 FY2027
Company unveiled the 'Range 500' aspiration - targeting combined group production of 500,000oz per annum within five years, positioning Capricorn as an emerging Australian multi-mine gold major

items.notes: Up from FY2026 actual production of 123,589oz; reflects contribution from KEP ramp-up during the year
Materially higher than FY2026 actual of $1,629/oz, reflecting KEP commissioning costs, higher strip ratios and cost inflation
Down sharply from FY2026's $300.7m combined KEP/MGGP spend as KEP nears completion; excludes potential MGGP construction capital once development formally commences
Subject to completion of remaining Western Australian state environmental/permitting approvals

guidance.management_commentary: Executive Chairman Mark Clark emphasized 'another outstanding year' with record financial results, reiterated the Range 500 aspiration (500,000ozpa within five years), and highlighted the strong balance sheet (debt-free, unhedged, $504.8m net cash) as providing capacity to fully fund both KEP and MGGP without external capital. Management flagged FY2027 as a transition year with elevated AISC from KEP commissioning before medium-term production and cost benefits are realized.

bull_case: Debt-free, unhedged balance sheet with $504.8m net cash fully funds both growth projects (KEP, MGGP) internally without shareholder dilution
MGGP PFS confirms a transformative, high-margin, 19-year mine life asset (260,000ozpa steady state, pre-tax NPV ~A$6.1bn at A$5,500/oz) that could more than triple group production once developed

Unhedged production gives full participation in a structurally bullish gold price environment (J.P. Morgan/Goldman Sachs forecasting $4,900-6,000+/oz through 2026-2027) driven by central bank buying and Fed easing
Maiden dividend (FY2026) signals capital return discipline alongside growth, broadening the investor base to income-focused holders while growth capex continues
Strong reserve/resource growth trajectory (Group Ore Reserves +1.2Moz to 5.2Moz in FY2026) with underground potential at both KGP and MGGP still being defined, suggesting further mine-life extension
bear_case: Single-mine production concentration (KGP) until MGGP ramps up leaves earnings highly exposed to any operational disruption, and FY2027 AISC guidance of $1,900-2,100/oz shows costs rising faster than production
Dual concurrent project execution (KEP commissioning plus MGGP construction start) raises the risk of delays, cost overruns, or capital misallocation typical of ambitious growth phases
No hedging means a gold price correction would hit margins directly and immediately, with AISC now structurally higher than in the FY2022-2023 period
MGGP remains subject to outstanding WA state environmental approvals; the targeted December 2026 quarter development start could slip if permitting is delayed

Rich valuation (analyst consensus target ~A$17.5-17.7 with 'Strong Buy' ratings already reflecting much of the growth optionality) leaves limited room for disappointment, and market cap (~$5-6bn) sits well below larger, more diversified peers like Northern Star and Evolution Mining that offer lower single-asset risk
